title: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the voxel-based soft-body simulation with randomly phased contractile cells, selection for locomotion produced morphologies that derandomize motion: shape and the distribution of passive and contractile cells evolved so the global movement was coherent despite random actuation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As a side effect of selection pressure for locomotion, derandomizing morphologies evolved: evolutionary improvement occurred through changes in overall shape, and distribution of the passive and contractile cells, to collectively derandomize the global movement produced by the random actuation.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Discussion”. Scope: Evolutionary design in a soft-body physics simulation of passive and contractile voxels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a computational result with explicit inputs and measurable outputs. The published simulation specification and artifacts make rerunning or reimplementing the selection experiment feasible without new biological data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run evolutionary searches under randomized actuator phases and measure directional coherence across generations, comparing evolved shapes and material layouts with ancestral, shuffled, and no-selection controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exact reproducibility depends on simulator version and random seeds.

Derandomization needs a prespecified coherence metric.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is about an outcome inside a specified soft-body evolutionary simulation, and the code for that simulation is public. A small team can re-evolve populations and measure whether shape and tissue arrangement reduce the randomness of global motion relative to unselected controls. That comparison confirms or refutes the derandomization result without new biological data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-evolve locomotion under randomly phased contractile voxels and track, across generations, shape plus the fraction of passive versus contractile cells against the variance of heading or centroid velocity; derandomization holds if coherence rises under selection and stays low in unselected controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Coherence must be defined from the supplement; several variance metrics could be computed.

The 2019 VoxCad build is finicky to compile, and exact seeds are needed to match historical runs.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.8
discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.75
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a voxel soft-body simulation where each contractile voxel's phase offset is random and fixed per clade (so selection can only change which voxels exist and which are contractile), selection for net displacement yields designs that move much farther than random designs under the same random actuation, and the gain depends on the evolved arrangement of passive and contractile voxels rather than on the particular phases.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, on the second-pass setting (water: reduced gravity plus drag; random fixed phases), over the independent evolutionary trials analysed: (a) the median ratio of final-champion net displacement to the mean displacement of random designs is >= 2, and >= 80% of champions exceed the 95th percentile of random designs; (b) shuffling which of the champion's voxels are contractile (same shape, same number of contractile voxels, same phase field, 20 shuffles) reduces displacement: median over champions of (median shuffled displacement / champion displacement) <= 0.7; (c) re-evaluating each champion's body under fresh random phase fields (20 draws) gives a median displacement above the 95th percentile of random designs for >= 70% of champions. Supports if (a), (b) and (c) all hold.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if (a) fails badly (median champion/random ratio <= 1.2, or < 50% of champions above the random 95th percentile), or if (b) shows no dependence on material layout (median shuffled/champion ratio >= 0.95) and (c) fails (champions under fresh phases at or below the random-design median for >= 50% of champions). Any other outcome is 'mixed'. If neither published outputs nor a working simulator (original or the simplified re-implementation below) can be run, verdict is inconclusive (data-unavailable or not-operationalizable).
